project.name: pactify
project.description: Portable, vendor-neutral protocol for multiple AI agents to collaborate in one git repo. Files in .pact/ are the bus; log.jsonl is the authoritative source, STATE.yml is a regenerable projection. v1 protocol is frozen, with a Go CLI (Cobra + MCP SDK) and a bash reference implementation driving it today.

nodes.summary: Drives Runner.Tick across t0, t0+29m, t0+30m, t0+59m, t0+60m to assert arming-only first tick, no early fire, boundary fire, and second-window fire for an every:30m schedule.

nodes.name: TestRunnerSkipsAlreadyRunning
nodes.summary: Verifies that a schedule whose fakeSpawn reports alreadyRunning is logged as a skip (not an error) and still increments the spawn-call counter exactly once.

nodes.name: TestRunnerDisabledNotFired
nodes.summary: Confirms that a disabled schedule produces zero spawn calls even after the interval has elapsed across multiple ticks.

nodes.name: TestRunnerReloadsFileEachTick
nodes.summary: Asserts that schedules added after Runner construction are picked up on subsequent ticks — arm-only first, then fire — proving per-tick reload semantics.

nodes.name: Validate
nodes.summary: Reports whether an expression parses as one of the supported `daily@HH:MM | every:Nh | every:Nm` forms by delegating to NextFire against time.Now().

nodes.name: NextFire
nodes.summary: Pure function returning the next strictly-after `now` fire time for a daily@HH:MM or every:N{h,m} expression, rejecting anything else with an error.

nodes.name: DefaultPath
nodes.summary: Returns the machine-level schedules.json path, honoring the PACTIFY_HOME environment variable and falling back to ~/.pactify/schedules.json.

nodes.name: Load
nodes.summary: Reads and JSON-unmarshals the schedule list from path, treating missing or whitespace-only files as an empty list (not an error).

nodes.name: Save
nodes.summary: Atomically writes the schedule list to path (tmp file + rename), creating the parent directory if missing and normalizing a nil slice to an empty array.

nodes.name: TestValidateTable
nodes.summary: Table-driven validation of Validate across representative valid expressions (daily times, every intervals, trimmed whitespace) and a broad set of invalid forms (out-of-range, unsupported units, cron syntax, negatives).

nodes.name: TestNextFireDaily
nodes.summary: Table-driven checks for NextFire on daily@HH:MM covering later-today, already-passed-today (cross-midnight), exact-match (strict-after), and month-boundary rollovers.

nodes.name: TestNextFireEvery
nodes.summary: Table-driven checks for NextFire on every:Nh|Nm including hour, sub-hour, cross-midnight, and 90-minute cases.

nodes.name: TestNextFireInvalid
nodes.summary: Smoke test asserting that NextFire returns a non-nil error for a clearly bogus expression.

nodes.name: TestLoadSaveRoundTrip
nodes.summary: End-to-end Load/Save check: missing file → empty list, then writes a two-entry schedule list, re-loads, and verifies field-level fidelity (id, feature, expr, enabled).

nodes.name: architecture.md

nodes.name: deployment.md
nodes.summary: Pactify hosted deployment reference documenting the one-Vercel / two-Fly-apps topology split by git branch (main→staging→production fast-forward), CI gate (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`), planned install paths (Go/Node), per-project usage, dev environment notes, and the independently deployed pactify.dev Astro site split into its own repo with vendored sync.

nodes.name: linx-coordination.md
nodes.summary: Cross-team coordination checklist between Pactify and linx for sharing `@pactify-apps/relay` and `@pactify-apps/wire` during multi-machine orchestration (M2–M5), enumerating additive `RpcRequest` type extensions (zero linx code changes), the two auth-hardening items linx must implement (server-side challenge nonce, machine provisioning validation), optional pairing confirmation, and recommended coordination windows.

nodes.name: onboarding.md
nodes.summary: Five-minute project onboarding guide covering pactify installation, agent registration (machine-level), `pactify setup` project bootstrap, planner-driven task planning, `pactify orchestrate` autonomous execution, `pactify finish --pr` delivery, seat-definition semantics (`id:roles:entry[:kind]`), and dashboard deployment with Cloudflare Tunnel + Access for public exposure.

nodes.name: operations.md
nodes.summary: Pactify day-2 operations reference covering daily dev workflow (`git pull` + `.agent/CURRENT.md`), troubleshooting (STATE.yml/log.jsonl drift, status-transition rules), relay enable/monitor/disable procedures using flags/env/Keychain, release flow (`./scripts/release.sh`), `pactify orchestrate` configuration (seat→kind, `verify:`, project gate, escalation), the manual half-auto alternative, and the coordination-authority P3 base-write contract.

nodes.name: plugin-publishing.md
nodes.summary: Maintainer-only manual for the `pact` Claude plugin covering three testing/release paths (local `--plugin-dir` dev load, self-hosted `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` one-click install, optional personal skills dir), a pact-plugin-specific test checklist, and the deferred Anthropic community-marketplace submission procedure, with explicit reminders about `PACT_AGENT_ID` inheritance and version alignment in `plugins/pact/.claude-plugin/plugin.json`.

nodes.name: release-process.md
nodes.summary: Trunk-based release process for the Pactify product (relay + Mission Control) using three fast-forward-only long-lived branches (`main` → `staging` → `production`), with explicit promote-and-deploy steps (Fly `relay`, Vercel preview/prod), shared-Neon branch separation, rollback via parent SHA, linx coordination rules, and a one-time Vercel/Fly/Neon setup checklist.

nodes.name: pact-protocol.md
nodes.summary: Frozen normative specification of the Pact Protocol v1 — defines the append-only event log format, the `.pact/` file contract, task and feature state machines, the two invariants (no self-accept, all-tasks-accepted-before-merge), seat identity, command verbs, and additive addenda for task dependencies and join-client provenance.

nodes.name: agentworks-wire.md
nodes.summary: Source-of-truth draft spec for the shared cloud layer used by Pactify and Linx: frozen v1 wire envelope (OperationalHeader/RunState/EncryptedBlob), account key derivation, envelope encryption, auth handshake, relay-blind pairing, golden vectors for cross-language contract, and the Go port checklist for `internal/cloudauth`.

nodes.name: account-sso.md
nodes.summary: Draft spec adding Google and GitHub SSO as an added identity layer to Pactify's zero-knowledge account model — the master-secret CLI path stays first-class, OAuth authenticates, and a separate mechanism supplies decryption keys; covers Prisma additions, relay OAuth endpoints, web sign-in/profile pages, and link/escrow flows in `internal/cloudauth`.

nodes.name: coordination-authority.md
nodes.summary: Draft spec addressing two dogfood incidents — make the integration point (base branch) and the coordination target (project) into explicit, named, lockable resources arbitrated by the `serve` broker; introduces Layer A (project addressing by name) and Layer B (base as single-writer integration lane) with phased P0–P3 acceptance.

nodes.name: driver-modernization.md

nodes.name: review-runtime-deepening.md

nodes.name: assign.bats

nodes.name: checkpoint.bats

nodes.name: doctor.bats

nodes.name: f1_branch_flow.bats
nodes.summary: bats tests for the F1 branch/commit discipline — `pact_join` creates and checks out the feature branch, `pact_checkpoint` commits the worker's work, and re-join is idempotent (crash-resume).

nodes.name: f3_entry_files.bats
nodes.summary: bats tests for F3 entry-file integrity — pact_init must preserve pre-existing content, re-bake must be idempotent, and writes must never leak through a symlinked entry file.

nodes.name: help.bats
nodes.summary: bats tests verifying that pact.sh help output lists every protocol verb and references the two protocol rules (no self-accept, no early merge).

nodes.name: helpers_core.bats

nodes.name: setup_pact_repo

nodes.name: init.bats

nodes.name: interop.bats

nodes.name: join.bats

nodes.name: merge.bats

layers.name: CLI Command Layer
layers.description: Cobra-based pactify CLI entry points at cmd/pactify/ — every user-facing verb (init, join, assign, checkpoint, accept, changes, merge, status, serve, mcp, doctor, etc.) is wired here and dispatched to the internal packages below.

layers.name: Core Protocol Engine
layers.description: Append-only log event engine, role/rule enforcement, event types, and the state projection that regenerates STATE.yml from log.jsonl — plus JSON Schemas and filesystem/git/lock primitives that the rest of the system depends on.

layers.name: Orchestration Engine
layers.description: Multi-agent driver loop (orchestrate + planner + ACP runner), fix-until-green critic, recipe/audit/registry/schedule/wizard/finish workflows — the package that turns the protocol log into a self-driving dev team.

layers.name: Agents & Seats
layers.description: Agent-kind registry, launch profiles, MCP wiring into per-agent config files, session/diffstat/stats/machine-id/token/secret bookkeeping — everything pactify needs to recognise and steer every supported agent.

layers.name: MCP Server & HTTP Serving
layers.description: External protocol adapters: the MCP server (internal/mcp) that exposes every pact verb as tools for AI agents, and the HTTP serving layer (internal/serve) that backs the Mission Control dashboard and remote clients.

layers.name: Cloud Relay Client (Go-side)
layers.description: Go-side client for the hosted zero-knowledge cloud relay — authentication, websocket transport, remote execution, and remote-machine registration that lets the CLI collaborate across machines.

layers.name: Web Dashboard (Mission Control)
layers.description: React 19 + Vite + xyflow Mission Control frontend at web/ — canvas visualisation of seats/features/tasks, command palette, agents panel, and other operator-facing UI.

layers.name: Cloud Monorepo (Relay & Shared TS Modules)
layers.description: pnpm workspace at cloud/ containing the Fastify zero-knowledge relay server (with Prisma schema and migrations), the shared wire/crypto/pact-project/relay-client libraries, Dockerfile stages, and Fly.io deploy manifests.

layers.name: Documentation & Protocol Specs
layers.description: All project documentation: top-level README and agent context files, architecture/operations/deployment/onboarding guides, frozen Pact Protocol v1 spec and draft specs, task spec stubs, and the project charter (PROJECT.md).

layers.name: Tests, Build & Distribution
layers.description: Bats CLI end-to-end tests, CI/release pipelines, root build configs (go.mod/.goreleaser/.mcp.json/opencode.json), the Claude/Gemini plugin distribution, the .pact runtime artifacts of the dev repo, the dogfood showcase, and the install/gitattributes scripts.

tour.title: Protocol at a Glance
tour.description: Start with the README narrative: pactify is a portable multi-agent coordination protocol where a git-tracked append-only event log (.pact/log.jsonl) is authoritative and STATE.yml is a regenerable projection. The formal spec defines events, roles, and the two invariants. Read these before any code to understand the story the rest of the tour retells through actual structure.

tour.title: The Event Log — the single source of truth
tour.description: The heart of the protocol lives in internal/event. An Event carries verb/actor/task/feature payloads; log.go appends events (stamping id + timestamp) and reads them back losslessly. Everything else is derived from this JSONL file, so understanding Append/ReadAll and the Event shape is foundational.

tour.title: Projection — folding events into STATE.yml
tour.description: internal/projection turns the log into state. Project/Fold replays events into the State/Feature/Task/Seat model; render.go serializes it byte-aligned to STATE.yml; snapshot.go accelerates replays. This is the 'log is source, STATE is projection, CLI recomputes' rule made concrete.

tour.title: Rules — the two invariants enforced
tour.description: rules.go encodes the protocol guarantees: a worker cannot self-accept (only the task's reviewer can), and a feature cannot merge until all its tasks are accepted. checkCheckpoint, checkReviewerVerdict, checkMerge, and the role gate are where correctness is guarded before any event is written.

tour.title: The Engine — verbs that mutate the ledger
tour.description: engine.go is the transactional core: each protocol verb (assign, start, checkpoint, changes, accept, merge, join) runs under a ledger lock, checks rules, then appends-and-renders atomically. This is where log, projection, and rules compose into safe state transitions.

tour.title: Seats & Roles — who may act
tour.description: seat.go models agent identities (seats) and their roles, and manages the pact-managed block baked into AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md. Combined with the role gate, seats decide which verbs an actor may perform — the identity layer behind the invariants.

tour.title: The CLI Surface
tour.description: cmd/pactify is the standard implementation of the protocol. main.go wires the root command; commands.go assembles subcommands (setup, join, assign, checkpoint, run, serve, mcp, orchestrate...). This is the primary human/agent entry point that drives the engine.

tour.title: Orchestration Engine — driving agents automatically
tour.description: internal/orchestrate runs the pull-based dispatch loop: it reads STATE, launches owner and reviewer agents, runs gates, handles rework/escalation, and merges when green. loop.go's Run is mission control's automation brain, turning the protocol into a self-driving workflow.

tour.title: MCP Server — protocol as agent tools
tour.description: internal/mcp exposes the protocol over the Model Context Protocol so any MCP-capable agent can participate. server.go serves tools (status/join/assign/checkpoint/accept/merge) and resources (pact://state, pact://log); tools.go registers them and resolves the target project.

tour.title: Web Dashboard — mission control
tour.description: web/ is the React+Vite dashboard. main.tsx boots the app, App.tsx composes the views, lib/api.ts talks to the serve API, and Canvas.tsx renders the live board. Per the canvas craft spec, node positions have exactly two writers and RF nodes only merge-by-id.

tour.title: Cloud Relay — remote coordination
tour.description: Cloud lets seats coordinate across machines. Go-side internal/cloudclient authenticates and holds sessions while internal/relaysock speaks the wire protocol; the TS relay server (cloud/relay) and relay-client persist and broadcast events. This mirrors the local engine over the network.

tour.title: CI/CD, Release & Tests
tour.description: The distribution and verification layer: ci.yml runs Go + web unit tests and Playwright e2e; release.yml + .goreleaser.yaml build the single static binary; install.sh delivers it. Protocol behavior is pinned by bats suites (protocol_v1, merge, checkpoint) plus web vitest — the double-green gate.
